samples.summary: Unrequested scope: an overlay-detection guard (OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR + capture-phase listener) beyond the issue plan, which also changes ←/→ behavior the issue listed as "Unchanged"
samples.evidence: The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:35) scopes image-viewer.tsx to "optional `onClose`; `Escape` calls it in the existing keydown handler (same input/contenteditable guard as ←/→)". The diff instead adds a 16-line Radix-internal selector list, a `hasOpenOverlay()` check applied to *all* keys, and switches the listener from bubble to capture (`window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true)`). Acceptance criterion "Unchanged: pdf/file layouts, ←/→ prev/next, zoom, download, share" (todo:22) no longer holds literally: arrow keys are now suppressed whenever any open dialog/menu/listbox/popper content exists, and the capture-phase registration reorders the viewer's handler ahead of every bubble-phase handler on the page. The behavior is defensible (and is documented in docs/design/image-viewer.md:175-183), but it is extra mechanism the issue did not ask for and is the riskiest part of the change.

samples.summary: Overlay detection couples a feature component to Radix internal DOM attributes; if it is worth having, it belongs next to the ui/ primitives rather than in the image viewer
samples.evidence: `'[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper] > [data-state="open"]:not([data-slot="tooltip-content"])'` encodes Radix's private markup contract in app/files/image-viewer.tsx. The repo already has a similar-in-spirit helper at a different layer (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-image-input.ts:166 `isPasteOwnedElsewhere()`, matching `[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal="true"]`) and a related check in app/spreadsheet/components/comments/CommentPopover.tsx:60-61. Three ad-hoc variants of "is a dismissable layer open?" now exist; a single helper beside components/ui/dialog.tsx would be the reuse point, and would keep the Radix-version coupling in one file.

samples.summary: The extracted hook de-duplicates only one of five copies of the same slug-fallback, and its placement under app/files/ blocks the other four from reusing it
samples.evidence: The exact `fallbackSlug ?? workspaces[0]?.slug` → `/w/:slug` else `/documents` fallback also appears inline at app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:81, app/board/board-detail.tsx:56, app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:112 and app/documents/document-detail.tsx:194. Extracting it into `app/files/use-documents-path.ts` makes the shared destination available to FileShell + the image viewer only; a cross-feature location (e.g. src/hooks/ or the workspaces module) would let the other four detail shells drop their copies. Not required by the issue, so minor.

samples.summary: Back-button/redirect destination and the sidebar's own "Documents" nav item can now disagree for the same page
samples.evidence: `items` (file-shell.tsx:71-87) uses `workspaceSlug` and falls back to `/documents` when the document's workspace is unknown, while `useDocumentsPath` falls back to the *first* workspace (`/w/first`). So with a document whose workspaceId is not in the user's workspace list, the sidebar "Documents" link points at /documents while the header back button and the not-found redirect go to /w/<first>. FileShell also still computes `currentWorkspace`/`workspaceSlug` separately from the hook, duplicating the lookup.
